content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapter 4. Supplemental: FlashAttention and systems papers on transformer efficiency.

This unit studies architecture families as computational patterns. MLPs emphasize dense matrix operations, CNNs exploit spatial locality, RNNs process sequences recurrently, and transformers trade parallel sequence processing for expensive attention and memory behavior. Students learn to connect inductive bias to input structure, then connect architecture to system behavior: parameter count, activation memory, arithmetic intensity, data movement, batching shape, parallelization strategy, and hardware fit.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: compare an MLP, CNN, RNN, and transformer for image, audio, time-series, and text workloads. Deliverable: architecture choice rationale with one system bottleneck for each.

concepts.name: Convolutional neural network
concepts.description: A neural network architecture that uses convolution operations, commonly for image or spatial data.

concepts.name: Recurrent neural network
concepts.description: A neural network architecture designed to process sequences by carrying state across time steps.

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.description: A neural network architecture based on attention mechanisms that is widely used for language, vision, and multimodal tasks.

concepts.name: Attention mechanism
concepts.description: A method that lets a model weight different input parts according to their relevance to the current computation.

concepts.name: Embedding
concepts.description: A learned numeric representation of an item, token, or category in a continuous vector space.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.description: A core linear algebra operation used heavily in neural network computation.

concepts.name: Computational graph
concepts.description: A graph representation of operations and data dependencies used for model execution and differentiation.

concepts.name: Parameter sharing
concepts.description: Using the same learned parameters in multiple places to reduce model size or encode repeated structure.
